long_biography.plain_text:
Building Kipany Productions from a film-production venture into a national direct-marketing agency was Tiffany Hendry's defining achievement. She co-founded the company with Kip Colligan in 1979 and served as president, combining creative production with client development and operational leadership. Its work for large businesses eventually spanned marketing, sales, communications and video production.

That business drew on a varied creative apprenticeship. After studying drama at Vanderbilt University and Boston College, Hendry trained at the Actors Studio in New York. She appeared in The Trojan Women in 1963 and became the sole white member of the Negro Ensemble Company before moving into recording and talent production. On returning east, she worked with Olympia Dukakis to organise the Whole Theater Company in New Jersey.
